title: Rehousing a dirty AND fails: in some AND/OR edge circuit, zeroing a dirty AND and serving its lost edges by stars and widened tops exceeds the count

plain_statement: False: G a graph, F its edge function, C AND/OR (two earlier wires each, so only earlier wires) computing F, g a dirty AND. Zero g; each edge then lost is served by a star x_c AND OR(O c), c in St an end, O c wires below the OR of c's neighbours, true at the edge; or by a top T in Tp (AND below F, ORs to the output) with one operand widened by ends U(T), T's other operand AND x_u below F. Dd: gates nobody reads; Fo: gates reading wires the zero forces false. Then an AND/OR circuit computes F with fewer dirty ANDs and at most |C| - 1 - |Dd| - |Fo| + sum_St (|O c| + 1) + sum_Tp |U(T)| gates.

counterexample.description: Its literal negation pair, L-meta-5397, is checked (run-048807); recorded by the hub in the same act.

faithful.note: Negation of L-meta-5397's term (script), but its sentence repeats 5397's dropped 'not in Dd' clause; refile with 5397.

corrections.note: The term asks more than the sentence: each O c wire is not g and not in Dd; Dd is gates other than g and the output, read only by g or by Dd; each top T is not g, not in Dd and not in Fo. Read 'O c wires' and 'Dd: gates nobody reads' that way.
